messages:
Priya: Ran the region+tier fallback SLA sims last night. Uploaded the raw numbers to the doc (link in thread). TL;DR: applying a cost-aware cheap-variant fallback for low-tier customers reduces token spend by ~30% under heavy traffic while keeping p95 latency within ~2x the baseline for most regions.

Mitch: can you share the sim inputs? what do you mean by 'cheap-variant fallback' exactly?

Priya: sure — cheap-variant = quantized/cheap model variant (gptj-quant8 in the sim). The sim tries the primary model, if queuing/capacity pushes expected token cost above per-request budget or latency would exceed soft SLO, it routes to the cheaper variant. Important: we modeled different region penalties (cross-region penalty + cold kv-cache penalty).

Jorge: interesting. rough question: does the 30% assume perfect prefix caching? cold starts could change that a lot.

Priya: good call — sims include a cold-fraction parameter per region (default 0.15). With cold=0.4 the cost savings drops to ~18% and p95 increases slightly. I added a table in the doc.

Aisha: posting the snippet of the policy we fed into the simulator for easy reference:

```json
{
  "routing_priority": ["customer_tier", "region_preference"],
  "fallbacks": {
    "low": ["gptj-quant8", "gptj-16"],
    "standard": ["gptj-16"],
    "enterprise": []
  },
  "token_cost_budget": {
    "low": 0.45,
    "standard": 0.9,
    "enterprise": 2.0
  },
  "region_penalty": {"eu": 1.05, "us-west": 1.0, "apac": 1.15}
}
```

Kevin: we should be careful: cheap variants have different hallucination profiles. How are we measuring output quality regression in these sims?

Priya: we included a proxy metric using our eval harness — per-prompt BLEU/ROUGE-ish deltas on a sampled prompt set (100k rows across customers). The sims flag cases where cheap variant drops quality beyond a threshold and mark them as "no-fallback" for that route. That reduced pure cost wins but prevented obvious regressions.

Mitch: operational concerns: when we route large % of traffic to cheap variants, their KV caches will warm differently and might skew p50/p95. Did you model continuous batching differences?

Priya: yes, batching differences modeled by variant throughput profiles. Cheap variants had higher throughput but lower token efficiency in some cases; we balance based on per-route latency SLO and a cost-per-token multiplier.

Jorge: metrics we need in Console to make this actionable: 1) per-route per-tier token spend, 2) per-variant p50/p95/p99, 3) quality/regression flags linked to prompt-sets, 4) rollback triggers when customer SLA violations exceed threshold.

Aisha: agree. I'll sketch a Console widget: lane for each tier showing current fallback mix, estimated monthly delta, and a heatmap for region penalties. Want to add an "explain route" pane that shows why a request was routed to variant X (token budget exceeded, region capacity, quality flag).

Kevin: for safety we should add a short-circuit: if a route's fallback rate > 20% for >10m, revert to standard routing and create an alert. Also, per-customer overrides (opt-out of cheap variants) must be honored.

Priya: added that to the sim policy and ran a sensitivity run — the auto-revert prevents long tail SLA blowups while still letting short spikes offload.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/variant-routing-sim v3 -> staging at 2026-03-18T09:00Z (dry-run).

Mitch: nice. action items: (1) Aisha to prototype Console widgets + explain route, (2) Jorge to add telemetry for per-variant quality deltas, (3) Kevin to draft safety revert alert thresholds, (4) Priya to run a 48h mixed-traffic sim with cold=0.35 and post results.

Aisha: will mock up widgets by end of week and add wire screenshots to the doc.

Jorge: I'll instrument the eval harness to push per-variant QA metrics to telemetry pipeline, ETA 2 weeks.

Kevin: I'll write up an alert playbook + default thresholds and add a runbook for oncall ops.

Priya: thanks all. putting follow-up sync on calendar for Thu to review the 48h sim. Link to doc: https://redwood.internal/sim-results/variant-routing-1803456789

Mitch: thumbs up :thumbsup:
